discovery: Discovery of the quantization of conductance in ballistic quantum point contacts

nominees.name: Bart J. van Wees
nominees.affiliation: Zernike Institute for Advanced Materials, University of Groningen, Netherlands

subfield: Condensed matter physics: mesoscopic quantum transport
motivation: In 1988 two independent experiments, by van Wees and co-workers (Delft/Philips) and by Wharam, Pepper and co-workers (Cambridge), showed that the conductance of a narrow constriction in a two-dimensional electron gas increases in steps of 2e^2/h as its width is tuned by a gate. This was a direct, striking demonstration that electrical conduction through a nanostructure is set by the number of transmitting quantum channels, confirming the Landauer-Buttiker picture of transport. The quantum point contact became the basic element of mesoscopic physics. It is used as a sensitive charge detector for spin and charge qubits, as the building block of electron quantum optics and quantum Hall interferometers, and as a spectroscopic probe of Andreev and Majorana states in hybrid superconductor-semiconductor devices. The discovery founded the field of engineered quantum electronic devices, and its influence on quantum technology keeps growing.
